correctness.rationale: The only scalar idempotents are 0 and 1. The nontrivial ones have scalar part 1/2 and vector part x/2 with Q(x)=1; a decomposition into two nonzero orthogonal idempotents cannot use the unit, and two proper parts would sum to scalar 1, so they are primitive. The ordered product determines s=x+y=4w and c=Q(s)/8. The change of variables x=s/2+z, y=s/2-z is a bijection to B(s,z)=0 and Q(z)=1-Q(s)/4. If s=0 the form is the original one; if s is nonisotropic the restriction has determinant D/Q(s); if s is nonzero isotropic, split off a hyperbolic plane of determinant -1 and count q lifts from a dimension-(d-2) form of determinant -D. Character orthogonality with G^2=chi(-1)q gives the stated even and odd signs, including the level zero, and the dimension-zero convention is necessary. Over an odd finite field, a nondegenerate form of dimension at least two represents every nonzero scalar and always represents zero by the zero vector. Thus all paraboloid targets occur at d>=4. In d=3 a nonzero isotropic s leaves a line representing 1 exactly when chi(-D)=1, giving 2q pairs then and none otherwise. The ternary zero level has q^2 vectors; the split d=2 case excludes every nonzero isotropic s. Bounded literal Cartesian-product checks agreed, including all 3,125 targets for each four-dimensional determinant class over F_5 and 24 omitted targets for the nonsplit-sign ternary example. The preserved replay paths are verify_idempotent_products.py and idempotent_output.txt beside RESULT.md; the frozen runs include characteristic-three and F_9 examples, not a universal certificate.
